questions.title: A 22-year-old woman at 16 weeks of her first pregnancy passes grape-like masses of tissue per vagina, having never felt fetal movement; the uterus measures large for dates, and D&C yields fluid-filled vesicles with avascular villi and trophoblastic proliferation on histology, consistent with a complete hydatidiform mole. What is the best method for her post-evacuation follow-up?
questions.question: A 22-year-old woman at 16 weeks of her first pregnancy passes grape-like masses of tissue per vagina, having never felt fetal movement; the uterus measures large for dates, and D&C yields fluid-filled vesicles with avascular villi and trophoblastic proliferation on histology, consistent with a complete hydatidiform mole. What is the best method for her post-evacuation follow-up?

options.A: Serial serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) monitoring
options.C: Routine pelvic ultrasound alone, without any tumor marker
options.D: A single beta-hCG level at 6 weeks post-evacuation, with no further follow-up if normal

explanations.A: Correct. Molar pregnancy is characterized by trophoblastic proliferation that produces very high levels of beta-hCG, and a defining part of its management is serial, regularly-scheduled serum beta-hCG monitoring after evacuation until it falls to and remains at an undetectable level, because a plateauing or rising titer signals persistent or malignant gestational trophoblastic disease (invasive mole or choriocarcinoma) requiring further treatment. Patients are also counseled to avoid pregnancy during this monitoring period, since a new pregnancy would itself raise hCG and confound interpretation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Alpha-fetoprotein is not the tumor marker produced by trophoblastic tissue; beta-hCG, produced by the proliferating trophoblast itself, is the relevant marker for molar pregnancy follow-up.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Ultrasound alone cannot reliably detect the microscopic, biochemical evidence of persistent trophoblastic disease that serial beta-hCG monitoring is designed to catch early.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A single early beta-hCG check is inadequate; the whole point of follow-up is serial monitoring over weeks to months to confirm the titer falls to and remains at zero, since persistent disease can declare itself later.

questions.learning_objective: Molar pregnancy follow-up requires serial serum beta-hCG monitoring after evacuation

questions.title: A prostatic carcinoma is diagnosed in a 70-year-old man. Which of the following statements about normal, benign prostatic acini is true regardless of the presence of cancer elsewhere in the gland?
questions.question: A prostatic carcinoma is diagnosed in a 70-year-old man. Which of the following statements about normal, benign prostatic acini is true regardless of the presence of cancer elsewhere in the gland?

options.A: With advancing age, they normally accumulate corpora amylacea — concentrically laminated proteinaceous concretions — within their lumina
options.B: They are normally lined by a single layer of malignant-appearing cells even in the absence of cancer
options.C: They characteristically lack a basal cell layer, identical to malignant glands
options.D: They normally show absent secretory activity throughout adult life

explanations.A: Correct. Corpora amylacea are eosinophilic, concentrically laminated proteinaceous concretions that accumulate within the lumina of normal, benign prostatic acini (particularly in the peripheral zone) with advancing age, and they are a feature of benign glandular aging rather than of malignancy. Their presence in a gland is actually more suggestive of a benign process, since malignant acini characteristically lack corpora amylacea, which is one histologic clue pathologists use, together with loss of the basal cell layer, to help distinguish cancerous from benign glands.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Normal benign prostatic acini are lined by a bilayer of secretory luminal cells and an underlying basal cell layer with bland, non-malignant cytology, not malignant-appearing cells.
explanations.C: Incorrect. It is malignant prostatic glands that characteristically lose the basal cell layer; benign acini retain an intact basal cell layer, which is one of the key features used to distinguish them from cancer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Benign prostatic epithelium remains secretory throughout adult life (contributing to seminal fluid), rather than being uniformly quiescent.

questions.title: The bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands are located within which anatomical compartment?
questions.question: The bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands are located within which anatomical compartment?

explanations.A: Correct. The paired bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands lie within the deep perineal pouch, embedded in the external urethral sphincter, and their ducts pass through the perineal membrane to open into the proximal (bulbar) part of the spongy urethra. This location, deep to the perineal membrane and between the two layers of the urogenital diaphragm, is what distinguishes them from the greater vestibular (Bartholin's) glands, their female homologue, which instead lie in the superficial perineal pouch. Their secretion, released during sexual arousal, helps lubricate and neutralize residual acidity in the urethra before ejaculation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The superficial perineal pouch contains structures such as the crura of the penis/clitoris, the bulb of the penis/vestibule, and the greater vestibular (Bartholin's) glands in females, not the bulbourethral glands.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The ischiorectal (ischioanal) fossa is a fat-filled space lateral to the anal canal, unrelated to the bulbourethral glands' location within the urogenital diaphragm.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The retropubic (Retzius) space lies anterior to the bladder and posterior to the pubic symphysis, a separate anatomical compartment from the perineum where the bulbourethral glands sit.

questions.title: The internal os of the uterus marks the anatomical junction between which two structures?
questions.question: The internal os of the uterus marks the anatomical junction between which two structures?

options.A: The body and the cervix of the uterus
options.C: The uterine cavity and the fallopian tube (uterotubal junction)

explanations.A: Correct. The internal os is the inner opening of the cervical canal, marking the anatomical and histological junction between the body (corpus) of the uterus above and the cervix below. It is a key landmark in obstetrics because its integrity (cervical competence) determines the risk of second-trimester pregnancy loss or preterm birth, and its effacement and dilation are staged during labor. It is distinguished from the external os, which is the opening of the cervical canal into the vagina at the opposite end of the cervix.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The junction between the cervix and the vagina is marked by the external os (and the vaginal fornices surrounding the cervix), not the internal os.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The uterotubal junction, where the fallopian tube opens into the uterine cavity, is an entirely separate landmark at the opposite, superior lateral, end of the uterus from the internal os.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The endometrium and myometrium are the two tissue layers of the uterine wall, a histological rather than a topographic cervical landmark, and unrelated to the internal os.

questions.title: Which of the following organisms is a classic cause of non-immune fetal hydrops when a pregnant woman is infected in the first half of pregnancy?
questions.question: Which of the following organisms is a classic cause of non-immune fetal hydrops when a pregnant woman is infected in the first half of pregnancy?

explanations.A: Correct. Maternal parvovirus B19 infection, particularly when acquired in the first half of pregnancy, is a classic cause of non-immune fetal hydrops: the virus infects and suppresses fetal erythroid progenitor cells, producing severe fetal anemia that in turn leads to high-output cardiac failure and generalized fluid accumulation (hydrops). Because the fetal marrow has limited reserve capacity earlier in gestation, the anemia and resulting hydrops are most severe with earlier infection. Serial fetal ultrasound monitoring and, when indicated, intrauterine transfusion are used to manage this risk.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Congenital rubella infection classically causes a triad of cardiac defects, cataracts, and sensorineural deafness (congenital rubella syndrome) rather than being the classic cause of non-immune hydrops from fetal anemia.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Congenital cytomegalovirus infection classically causes periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, and sensorineural hearing loss; it can rarely contribute to hydrops but is not the classic teaching association for it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Congenital varicella syndrome classically causes limb hypoplasia, cutaneous scarring, and CNS/eye abnormalities, not the classic teaching cause of non-immune fetal hydrops.
